description: Smoke test for the self-instrumenting LGTM stack (pnpm run server:lgtm). Every panel reads a signal the stack produced about itself: Loki holds the five containers' stdout, Prometheus scrapes their /metrics, and Tempo's metrics-generator turns their traces into span metrics and service-graph edges. If all five panels have data, all four signals are wired.

options.content:
There is no data generator in this stack — **the stack is the workload.** Grafana running this dashboard is what makes these lines move: each refresh is an HTTP request Prometheus counts, a query Loki logs, and a trace Tempo turns into service-graph edges.

A quiet stack is a flat dashboard. Pan the time picker or open a few dashboards to give it something to measure.

panels.description: Logs: Alloy tails each container's stdout over the Docker socket and pushes it to Loki. `service_name` is the Compose service name.
panels.title: Log lines/sec by service — Loki

panels.description: Metrics: Prometheus scrapes /metrics on all five containers, including itself. Resident memory is used here because it is the one series every service in the stack exposes.
panels.title: Resident memory by service — Prometheus

panels.description: Traces, twice removed: the services export OTLP to Tempo, Tempo's metrics-generator derives service-graph edges from those traces, and remote-writes them to Prometheus as traces_service_graph_request_total{client,server}. label_replace renames the pair to source/target, which is the graph-*-wide contract the relations panel reads — no transformations needed. This is the same query shape as provisioning/dashboards/relations/devcortex-wide.json, against a stack you can run locally.
panels.title: Service graph — Tempo metrics-generator via Prometheus

panels.description: The other metrics-generator output: span metrics. One series per traced service, so it doubles as the check that a service's OTLP export is actually reaching Tempo.
panels.title: Spans/sec by service — Tempo span metrics

panels.description: The raw lines behind the first panel. Loki derives `detected_level` itself, and the Loki datasource is provisioned with a derived field on traceID, so a dskit log line links straight into its trace in Tempo.
panels.title: Stack logs — Loki

title: LGTM stack — self-instrumented
